binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is an implicitly quantified measure on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
S is an implicitly quantified function Ω → ℝ.
λ and t are implicitly universally quantified real numbers.
hypotheses: S is measurable from Ω to the Borel measurable space on ℝ.
The function ω ↦ exp(λ·S(ω)) is integrable with respect to μ.
conclusions: The real-valued μ-measure of {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) ≥ t} equals the real-valued μ-measure of {ω ∈ Ω | exp(λ·S(ω)) ≥ exp(λ·t)}.
The real-valued μ-measure of {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) ≥ t} is at most exp(-λ·t) multiplied by ∫ exp(λ·S(ω)) dμ(ω).
Both preceding conclusions hold simultaneously as a conjunction.
mathematical_definitions: For a set A, the expression μ.real(A) is toReal(μ(A)), the real conversion of the extended nonnegative measure value.
Let M_λ = ∫_Ω exp(λ·S(ω)) dμ(ω). Then the asserted bound is μ.real(A_t) ≤ exp(-λ·t)·M_λ.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable real-valued function S on a space carrying a measure μ with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance, and for every real threshold t and positive real λ such that exp(λS) is μ-integrable, the measure of the upper-tail event S ≥ t equals the measure of the transformed event exp(λS) ≥ exp(λt), and this tail measure is at most exp(-λt) times the integral of exp(λS) with respect to μ.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result is conditional on λ > 0; it states nothing for λ = 0 or λ < 0.
There is no sign restriction on t and no boundedness, centering, independence, or moment assumption on S beyond measurability and integrability of exp(λS).
The conclusion is a conjunction, so the event-measure equality is part of the proposition rather than merely an unstated rewriting used to derive the inequality.
The event notation uses closed upper intervals, hence ≥ rather than >.

MeasureTheory.Measure.real converts an extended nonnegative measure value with toReal. If an event could have infinite measure, this conversion can obscure extended-value behavior; the usual probability-measure interpretation would make all event measures finite, but the dossier does not expose the IsProbabilityMeasure fields needed to verify that internally.
If the measurability, positivity, integrability, or implicit measure-class assumptions are not satisfiable for particular data, the implication is vacuously true for those data.
The bound is asserted for each admissible λ separately; the proposition does not optimize over λ.
No logarithm, expectation notation, or separately named moment-generating function is encoded.
ambiguities: The exact semantic fields of the IsProbabilityMeasure typeclass are absent. Calling μ a probability measure uses the conventional meaning of that identifier rather than a definition recoverable from the packet.

The internal definitions and axioms of MeasurableSpace and Measure are omitted; their standard mathematical roles are clear from their interfaces, but their exact encodings are not reconstructible here.

The implementation body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque in the packet. Its type identifies the real-valued Bochner integral interface, and the integrability hypothesis places this use in the integrable regime, but the underlying construction is not exposed.
The packet does not expose the behavior of the toReal conversion used by Measure.real, especially on an infinite extended value.
